 By : CNBCTV18.com November 16, 2026 | 05:00 IST Edited by Priyanka Deshpande 
 Published On Nov 16, 2026 | 05:00 IST 
 Last Updated On Nov 16, 2026 | 05:00 IST

 Summary A depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm on November 16, with the IMD issuing wind warnings. Rainfall is forecast in parts of southern, northeastern and eastern India, while Uttar Pradesh is likely to experience dense fog.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source A depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm on Monday, November 16, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The system is expected to strengthen further over the following days and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. Meanwhile, several parts of the country are likely to receive rainfall, while dense fog conditions are forecast over Uttar Pradesh.
 Bay of Bengal depression likely to intensify into cyclonic storm 
 The depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is moving north-northwestwards and is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal on November 16.
 According to the IMD, the system is expected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal on November 17. It is then likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast over the following two days.
 The system was located around 800 km east-southeast of Chennai and 960 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam at 11.30 am on November 15.
 Wind warning over Bay of Bengal and coastal areas 
 The IMD has warned of strengthening winds over the Bay of Bengal as the depression intensifies.
 On November 16, squally winds reaching 55-65 kmph, gusting to 75 kmph, are likely over the southeast Bay of Bengal from the morning. These are expected to strengthen into gale-force winds reaching 60-70 kmph, gusting to 80 kmph, from noon.
 Over the southwest Bay of Bengal, squally winds reaching 55-65 kmph, gusting to 70 kmph, are likely from the morning. Gale-force winds reaching 65-75 kmph, gusting to 85 kmph, are forecast from noon.
 Over the central Bay of Bengal, winds reaching 45-55 kmph, gusting to 65 kmph, are likely on November 16. These are expected to strengthen into gale-force winds reaching 60-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph, from the evening.
 Along and off the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts, squally winds reaching 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are likely until November 17. Wind speeds are expected to increase thereafter.
 IMD issues fishermen warning 
 In its November 15 advisory, the IMD had asked fishermen out at sea to return to the coast by that day. Fishermen have also been advised not to venture into the following areas: 
 Andaman Sea and along and off the Andaman and Nicobar Islands until November 17.
 Southeast Bay of Bengal until November 17.
 Southwest Bay of Bengal from November 15 to 19.
 Central Bay of Bengal from November 16 to 20.
 Northwest Bay of Bengal on November 19 and 20.
 IMD weather forecast for November 16: Rainfall in these regions 
 The IMD has forecast isolated to scattered rainfall over the following regions on Monday:
 South India: Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Rayalaseema and Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
 Northeast India: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya.
 East India: Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim.
 Andaman and Nicobar Islands: Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall is likely.
 Dense fog warning for Uttar Pradesh 
 The IMD has forecast dense fog conditions over Uttar Pradesh from November 15 to 17.
 Very dense fog, with visibility below 200 metres, was reported at isolated places in the state during the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on November 15. Bareilly, Kushinagar, Ayodhya and Azamgarh were among the locations that reported poor visibility.
 The weather agency has warned that dense fog could affect airports, highways and railway routes in the state. It has advised people to exercise caution while travelling, use fog lights while driving and check with airlines and railway services for updates on their journeys.
 Delhi weather forecast for November 16 
 Delhi is likely to witness mainly clear skies on Monday, November 16, with mist or shallow fog at most places and moderate fog at a few places during the morning hours.
 The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to remain between 26-28 degrees Celsius and 14-16 degrees Celsius, respectively. The maximum temperature is expected to remain below normal at most places, while the minimum temperature is likely to be near normal.
 Northwesterly winds are likely to reach speeds of up to 10 kmph during the morning and increase to 20 kmph during the afternoon before weakening to around 10 kmph during the evening and night.
